questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in AM) between 2 AM and 3 AM will the hour and minute hands of the clock be opposite to each other?
questions.solution:
At **2 AM**, the position of the hands is:

Minute hand = 0° (at 12)

Hour hand = 2 × 30° = 60° (at 2)

Initial angle between hands = 60°

To be **opposite**, the minute hand must cover the initial 60° gap and gain another 180° relative to the hour hand.

Total angular distance to be covered = 60° + 180° = 240°

Time taken = Distance ÷ Relative speed

Time = 240 ÷ 5.5 = 480 ÷ 11 minutes

Time ≈ 43.636 minutes

Approximating to the nearest minute, we get **44 minutes**.

Therefore, the time is approximately **2:44 AM**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The angle θ between the **hour hand** and **minute hand** is given by the formula:

 theta = | (60H - 11M)/(2) | 

Where **H** = hours and **M** = minutes.

Given **H = 2** and **θ = 180°** (for opposite hands):

180 = | (60 × 2 − 11 × M) ÷ 2 |

360 = | 120 − 11M |

Since the minute hand must pass the hour hand to be opposite, we take the case where 11M > 120:

360 = 11M − 120

480 = 11M

M = 480 ÷ 11 ≈ 43.64 minutes

Hence, the correct answer is **2:44**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] __Important Points__** __​__The hour hand of a clock covers 360° in 12 hours.

Angular distance covered in 1 hour = 360 ÷ 12 = 30°

Angular distance covered in 1 minute = 30 ÷ 60 = 0.5°

The minute hand covers 360° in 60 minutes.

Angular distance covered in 1 minute = 360 ÷ 60 = 6°

The relative speed of the minute hand with respect to the hour hand = 6° − 0.5° = 5.5° per minute.

Two hands are opposite to each other when the angle between them is 180°.

questions.question: The ratio of present ages of S and T is 5 : 3. After 2 years, their ages will be in the ratio of 7 : 5. What will be the age of S after 3 years from present?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is based on the **ratio** and **ages** calculation.

Let the **present age** of **S** be 5x and the **present age** of **T** be 3x.

**Ages after 2 years:**

Age of **S** = 5x + 2

Age of **T** = 3x + 2

According to the question, the **ratio of their ages after 2 years** will be **7 : 5**.

(5x + 2) / (3x + 2) = 7 / 5

By **cross-multiplication:**

5 × (5x + 2) = 7 × (3x + 2)

25x + 10 = 21x + 14

25x − 21x = 14 − 10

4x = 4

**x = 1**

Now, we find the **present age of S:**

Present age of S = 5x = 5 × 1 = **5 years**

The question asks for the **age of S after 3 years** from the present:

Age after 3 years = Present age + 3

Age after 3 years = 5 + 3 = 8 years

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 1**”.

questions.question: What is the speed of sound in air at 0°C?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**331 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sound is a **mechanical longitudinal wave** that requires a material medium like air, water, or steel for its propagation.
 
• The speed of sound in a gas is primarily dependent on the **temperature** and the **density** of the medium.
 
• At a standard temperature of **0°C** (equivalent to **273.15 K**), the speed of sound in dry air is measured to be approximately **331 m/s**.
 
• This value is derived using the **Laplace correction** to Newton's formula, which considers the propagation of sound as an **adiabatic process**. The formula is expressed as v = √(γRT/M), where γ is the **adiabatic index**, R is the **universal gas constant**, T is the **absolute temperature**, and M is the **molar mass** of the gas.
 
• In air, which consists mainly of **nitrogen** and **oxygen**, the speed is relatively low compared to solids and liquids because gases have much lower **elasticity** and higher **compressibility**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Impact of Temperature:**

 
 
• The speed of sound is directly proportional to the **square root of absolute temperature**.
 
• For every **1°C** rise in temperature, the speed of sound increases by approximately **0.61 m/s**.
 
• At **20°C** (standard room temperature), the speed of sound increases to approximately **343 m/s** or **344 m/s**.
 
• At **25°C**, the speed further reaches approximately **346 m/s**.
 
 
 
• **Humidity and Density:**
 
 
• **Humidity** increases the speed of sound because moist air is less dense than dry air. Since speed is inversely proportional to the square root of **density**, lower density results in higher velocity.
 
• Changes in **atmospheric pressure** do not affect the speed of sound provided the temperature remains constant, as the density changes proportionally to the pressure.
 
 
 
• **Speed in Different Media:**
 
 
• Sound travels fastest in **solids** (e.g., approximately **5960 m/s** in steel) due to high bulk modulus.
 
• Sound travels at an intermediate speed in **liquids** (e.g., approximately **1480 m/s** in water at 20°C).

questions.question: Which region of India is called the "Roof of the World"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ladakh Plateau**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ladakh Plateau** is widely recognized as the **Roof of the World** in the context of Indian geography because it is the highest plateau in India, acting as a southward extension of the **Tibetan Plateau**.
 
• It is a **trans-Himalayan** landmass situated at an average elevation of more than **3,000 meters** (approximately **9,800 feet**), with some areas exceeding **5,000 meters**.
 
• Geographically, it is located between the **Karakoram Range** in the north and the **Great Himalayan Range** in the south, forming a high-altitude **cold desert**.
 
• The plateau covers a vast area of approximately **59,146 square kilometers** and is characterized by its high-altitude plains, such as the **Depsang Plains** and the **Aksai Chin** region.
 
• Due to the **rain-shadow** effect of the Himalayas, the region receives very little rainfall, averaging around **100 mm** annually, leading to its unique arid and barren landscape.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deccan Plateau**:

 
 
• A large **volcanic plateau** covering most of South India, formed by **basaltic lava flows** during the **Cretaceous** period.
 
• It is bounded by the **Satpura Range** in the north and the **Western and Eastern Ghats** on the sides.
 
 
 
• **Chotanagpur Plateau**:
 
 
• Located in Eastern India, primarily in **Jharkhand**, it is a **continental plateau** composed of ancient **Archean rocks**.
 
• Known as the **Ruhr of India** due to its immense wealth of minerals like **coal**, **iron ore**, and **bauxite**.
 
 
 
• **Malwa Plateau**:
 
 
• Situated in central-western India, it forms a part of the **Central Highlands** and is drained by the **Chambal River** system.
 
• It consists of **black soil**, which is highly suitable for growing **cotton** and **oilseeds**.

questions.question: In which city was the 8th BRICS Summit held in 2016?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goa, India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **8th BRICS Summit** was held in **Benaulim, Goa, India**, on **15 and 16 October 2016**. This marked the second time **India** hosted the summit, following the **4th BRICS Summit** in **New Delhi** in **2012**.
 
• The theme for the 2016 summit was **Building Responsive, Inclusive and Collective Solutions**. The event focused on enhancing cooperation in areas such as **trade**, **investment**, **security**, and **sustainable development**.
 
• The summit was attended by the heads of state/government of the five member nations: **Michel Temer** (Brazil), **Vladimir Putin** (Russia), **Narendra Modi** (India), **Xi Jinping** (China), and **Jacob Zuma** (South Africa).
 
• The meeting concluded with the adoption of the **Goa Declaration**, which strongly condemned **terrorism** in all its forms and manifestations, stressing that there can be no ideological, religious, or political justification for such acts.
 
• A major highlight was the **BRICS-BIMSTEC Outreach Summit** held on the sidelines, where leaders from **BIMSTEC** countries (Bangladesh, Bhutan, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, and Thailand) were invited to strengthen regional integration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ufa, Russia**:

 
 
• Hosted the **7th BRICS Summit** in **July 2015**.
 
• It was significant for the official operationalization of the **New Development Bank (NDB)** and the **Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA)**.
 
 
 
• **Johannesburg, South Africa**:
 
 
• The city hosted the **10th BRICS Summit** in **2018** and the **15th BRICS Summit** in **August 2023**.
 
• The 2023 summit was historic for announcing the **expansion** of the group to include new member nations.
 
 
 
• **Beijing, China**:
 
 
• **China** hosted the **14th BRICS Summit** in **2022** via video link.
 
• Other Chinese cities that hosted summits include **Sanya (2011)** and **Xiamen (2017)**.
 
 
 
• **BRICS Formation**:
 
 
• The acronym **BRIC** was originally coined by **Jim O'Neill** in **2001**.
 
• The group was formally constituted in **2006**, and **South Africa** joined the group in **2010**.

questions.question: What was a positive effect of liberalization and globalization on Indian industry?

options.text: Decline in efficiency due to competition
Access to advanced technology and larger markets
Complete withdrawal of the state from infrastructure

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Access to advanced technology and larger markets**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **New Economic Policy (NEP)** introduced in **1991** was a response to the severe **Balance of Payments (BoP)** crisis, shifting India from a closed economy to a more integrated, market-oriented one.
 
• **Liberalization** involved the dismantling of the **License Raj**, allowing Indian firms to expand production capacities and import modern machinery without the previous bureaucratic hurdles.
 
• **Globalization** facilitated the inflow of **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**, which acted as a vehicle for the transfer of **cutting-edge technology** and superior managerial practices from developed economies.
 
• Indian industries gained access to **larger markets** through the reduction of **tariff and non-tariff barriers**, enabling domestic brands to compete on a global scale and improve their **export performance**.
 
• Integration with the **world economy** encouraged Indian entrepreneurs to innovate, leading to a significant increase in the quality and diversity of goods available in the domestic market.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **LPG Reforms (1991)**:

 
 
• **Liberalization**: It aimed to promote **free-market competition** by removing government controls over prices and production in several industrial sectors.
 
• **Privatization**: Involved the **disinvestment** of public sector undertakings (PSUs) to improve operational efficiency through private ownership.
 
• **Globalization**: Encouraged the free flow of capital, goods, and services across international borders, aligned with the principles of the **World Trade Organization (WTO)**.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Efficiency**:
 
 
• Contrary to a decline, competition from **Multinational Corporations (MNCs)** forced Indian firms to adopt **cost-effective production** and improve **research and development (R&D)**.
 
 
 
• **Role of the State**:
 
 
• The government did not completely withdraw from infrastructure but shifted its role from a direct provider to a **facilitator and regulator**, utilizing models like **Public-Private Partnership (PPP)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **commanding heights** was used to describe the strategic sectors of the economy that were intended to remain under **State control** to ensure social justice and rapid economic development.
 
• During the period of **1950-1980**, India followed a **socialist-inspired** economic model where the **Public Sector** was assigned the lead role in industrialization.
 
• The **Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956** (IPR 1956) explicitly categorized **heavy industries**, **iron and steel**, **atomic energy**, and **heavy machinery** as sectors reserved exclusively for the government.
 
• These industries were considered **strategic** because they provided the basic infrastructure and raw materials required for the growth of all other sectors, including the private sector.
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan**, formulated by **P.C. Mahalanobis**, prioritized these capital-intensive industries to build a foundation for **long-term self-reliance** and to reduce dependence on foreign imports for basic industrial goods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Mahalanobis Model**:

 
 
• This economic strategy focused on the **development of capital goods** rather than consumer goods to accelerate the rate of **capital formation**.
 
• It was based on the premise that a **strong industrial base** in steel and energy would automatically pull the rest of the economy forward through **linkage effects**.
 
 
 
• **Reason for State Dominance**:
 
 
• **High Investment**: Heavy industries required massive financial outlays that the **Indian private sector** lacked during the post-independence era.
 
• **Long Gestation Periods**: These projects took a long time to become profitable, making them unattractive to private entrepreneurs seeking quick returns.
 
 
 
• **Other Sectors during 1950-1980**:
 
 
• **Agriculture**: Though it contributed the most to **GDP** and employment, it was not classified as the commanding heights as it was largely in the **private hands** of millions of farmers.
 
• **Textiles and Handicrafts**: These were classified as **consumer goods** or small-scale industries and did not possess the strategic control over the economy that **steel and energy** did.

questions.question: Which type of unemployment is due to technological progress?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Structural**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Structural unemployment** is a form of involuntary unemployment caused by a mismatch between the **skills** that workers in the economy can offer and the skills demanded of workers by employers.
 
• **Technological progress** is a primary driver of this phenomenon; as industries adopt **automation**, **robotics**, and **artificial intelligence**, traditional roles involving manual or routine labor become obsolete.
 
• This type of unemployment is considered **long-term** and chronic because it requires the displaced workforce to undergo significant **reskilling** or **vocational training** to fit into new sectors.
 
• Economic theories, such as **Creative Destruction**, suggest that while technology destroys old jobs, it creates new ones that require a different set of **technical competencies**.
 
• According to reports by the **World Economic Forum**, the rapid pace of the **Fourth Industrial Revolution** is expected to displace millions of roles, making structural unemployment a critical challenge for **labor market policy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seasonal Unemployment**:

 
 
• This occurs when demand for labor changes across different periods of the year. It is highly prevalent in the **agricultural sector** (during harvest/sowing) and the **tourism industry**.
 
 
 
• **Disguised Unemployment**:
 
 
• Refers to a situation where more people are working than necessary. In this case, the **marginal productivity** of the extra labor is **zero**. It is a common feature of **overpopulated developing economies**.
 
 
 
• **Frictional Unemployment**:
 
 
• A temporary phase where individuals are **between jobs** or are looking for their first job. It is often **voluntary** and reflects the time needed to match a worker with the right employer in a **dynamic economy**.

questions.question: In Tamil Bhakti literature, Vaishnava saints were called ______.

• The **Alvars** were **Tamil poet-saints** of **South India** who lived between the **6th and 9th centuries CE** and propagated the **Bhakti movement** through their intense devotion to **Lord Vishnu**.
 
• The word **Alvar** means **one who is immersed** in the love and experience of the Divine, signifying their complete surrender to **Vaishnavism**.
 
• There were **twelve Alvars** in total, coming from diverse social backgrounds, which highlighted the **inclusive nature** of the **Bhakti tradition** in medieval India.
 
• Their collective hymns, totaling **4,000 verses**, were compiled by **Nathamuni** in the **10th century** into a sacred canon known as the **Nalayira Divya Prabandham**.
 
• Prominent members included **Periyalvar**, **Nammalvar**, and **Andal**, the only female saint among the twelve, who is celebrated for her poetic works like **Thiruppavai**.

• **Nayanars**:

 
 
• These were a group of **63 saints** devoted to **Lord Shiva** who lived during the same period as the Alvars.
 
• Their lives and works were documented in the **Periyapuranam**, and their hymns form the **Tirumurai**, which is central to **Shaiva Siddhanta**.
 
 
 
• **Tirthankara**:

• There are **24 Tirthankaras** in the present cosmic age, beginning with **Rishabhanatha** and ending with **Mahavira**.

questions.question: Main Worker in India is a person who works for at least ____ days in a year.
questions.solution:

• In the **Census of India**, the population is divided into workers and non-workers based on their participation in economically productive activities.
 
• A **Main Worker** is defined as a person who has worked for the major part of the reference year, which is specifically at least **six months** or **183 days**.
 
• This classification was prominently established during the **1981 Census** to differentiate between steady employment and seasonal or temporary work.
 
• The duration of work includes both physical and mental activities and involves not only actual work but also effective supervision and direction of work.
 
• The identification of **Main Workers** helps the government calculate the **Workforce Participation Rate (WPR)** and understand the core economic stability of the country.

• A person who worked for less than **183 days** (or six months) in the reference year is categorized as a **Marginal Worker**.
 
• This group often includes seasonal laborers in the **agricultural sector** or individuals in the informal economy.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Categories of Workers**:
 
 
• **Cultivators**: Individuals engaged in cultivation on land owned or leased from the government or private institutions.
 
• **Agricultural Labourers**: Those who work on another person's land for wages without any right of lease or contract.
 
• **Household Industry Workers**: Persons working in industries such as processing, servicing, or manufacturing conducted by household members within the home or village.

• **Ramadan** is the **ninth month** of the **Islamic Hijri calendar**, during which believers observe **Sawm** (fasting) from dawn to sunset, abstaining from food and drink.
 
• The celebration begins on the first day of **Shawwal**, the month following Ramadan, and its timing is determined by the specific sighting of the **crescent moon** (Hilal).
 
• A mandatory charitable contribution known as **Zakat al-Fitr** is given to the poor before the special **Eid prayer** (Salat al-Eid), ensuring that all members of the community can celebrate the occasion.
 
• The day is marked by **communal prayers**, family gatherings, feasting, and the giving of gifts, symbolizing spiritual renewal and gratitude to **Allah** for the strength provided during the fasting month.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bakrid (Eid-al-Adha)**:

 
 
• Known as the **Feast of Sacrifice**, it honors the willingness of **Prophet Ibrahim** (Abraham) to sacrifice his son as an act of obedience to God.
 
• It falls on the **10th day** of **Dhu al-Hijjah**, the final month of the Islamic calendar, and marks the end of the **Hajj** pilgrimage.
 
 
 
• **Muharram**:
 
 
• This is the **first month** of the Islamic calendar; the 10th day is known as **Ashura**.
 
• For **Shia Muslims**, it is a day of intense mourning to commemorate the martyrdom of **Imam Hussain**, the grandson of **Prophet Muhammad**, at the **Battle of Karbala** in 680 AD.
 
 
 
• **Shab-e-Barat**:
 
 
• Often referred to as the **Night of Fortune** or **Night of Records**, it is observed on the night between the **14th and 15th** of the month of **Sha'ban**.
 
• It is a night of prayer and seeking forgiveness, as it is believed that **Allah** determines the destiny and provides for all creatures for the year ahead during this night.

questions.question:

• Many chemical industries rely heavily on **natural minerals** extracted from the earth or sea. **Salts**, **sulphur**, and **potash** are essential mineral inputs used to produce chemicals like **sulphuric acid**, **fertilizers**, and **industrial salts**. • **Inorganic Chemicals**:
 
 
• Includes **sulphuric acid** (used for fertilizers, plastics, paints), **nitric acid**, **alkalis**, **soda ash** (used for glass, soaps, detergents), and **caustic soda**.
 
• These industries utilize **natural minerals** like **rock phosphate**, **sulphur**, and **magnesium** as their primary raw materials.

questions.question: Which of the following number is neither divisible by 3 nor by 11?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Quickly check the **sum of digits** for divisibility by 3: **9999** (36), **10032** (6), and **9042** (15) are all multiples of 3.

Only **10019** has a sum of digits = 11, which is not **divisible by 3**.

Check **10019** for 11: (1 + 0 + 9) − (0 + 1) = 9, which is not **divisible by 11**.

**∴ The correct answer is 10019.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers are 10019, 9999, 10032, and 9042.

**Formula:** **Divisibility by 3** (Sum of digits) and **Divisibility by 11** (Alternating sum of digits).

**Checking for 3:**

⇒ 10019: 1 + 0 + 0 + 1 + 9 = 11 (Not divisible by 3)

⇒ 9999: 9 + 9 + 9 + 9 = 36 (Divisible by 3)

⇒ 10032: 1 + 0 + 0 + 3 + 2 = 6 (Divisible by 3)

⇒ 9042: 9 + 0 + 4 + 2 = 15 (Divisible by 3)

**Checking for 11:**

⇒ 10019: (Sum of digits at odd places) − (Sum of digits at even places)

⇒ (1 + 0 + 9) − (0 + 1) = 10 − 1 = 9 (Not divisible by 11)

Since **10019** fails both tests, it is the required number.

**∴ The correct answer is 10019.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is **divisible by 3** if the sum of all its digits is divisible by 3.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is **divisible by 11** if the difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

Divisibility by 33

If a number is divisible by both **3** and **11**, it is also divisible by 33 (e.g., 9999, 10032, and 9042).

questions.question: 156 chips and 234 toffees are to be distributed among maximum number of boys. Each boy gets the same number of chips. Each boy get the same number of toffees. How many chips does each boy get?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **maximum number of boys**, calculate the **HCF** of 156 and 234.

**HCF**(156, 234) = 78 (Since 156 = 78 × 2 and 234 = 78 × 3).

Number of chips each boy gets = **Total Chips** ÷ **Maximum Boys**.

Chips per boy = 156 ÷ 78 = 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total **Chips** = 156

Total **Toffees** = 234

Condition: **Maximum number** of boys with **equal distribution**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4cd9f05f7622355b1a790f4af83ad3770230d7c1663fb83c665d04953244a2de.png] 

**Step 1: Calculate HCF using Prime Factorization**

⇒ 156 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 13 = 2² × 3¹ × 13¹

⇒ 234 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 13 = 2¹ × 3² × 13¹

⇒ **HCF** = 2¹ × 3¹ × 13¹ = 2 × 3 × 13 = 78

**Step 2: Find chips per boy**

⇒ **Maximum boys** = 78

⇒ **Chips per boy** = 156 ÷ 78

⇒ **Chips per boy** = 2

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The **HCF** of two or more numbers is the largest number that divides each of them without leaving a remainder. It is used to find the **maximum size** or **maximum number** in distribution problems.

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their **HCF** and **LCM**: a × b = **HCF**(a, b) × **LCM**(a, b).

Division Method for HCF

Divide the larger number by the smaller one. If there is a remainder, divide the previous divisor by this remainder. Repeat until the remainder is zero; the last divisor is the **HCF**.

questions.question: A person spends 50 percent of his income. His income increases by 40 percent and expenditure increases by 30 percent. The increased saving is Rs. 7500. What is his initial income?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Income** : **Expenditure** : **Savings** = 100 : 50 : 50 = 2 : 1 : 1.

New **Income** = 2 × 140% = 2.8 units.

New **Expenditure** = 1 × 130% = 1.3 units.

**New Savings** = 2.8 − 1.3 = 1.5 units.

1.5 units = Rs. 7500 ⇒ 1 unit = Rs. 5000.

**Initial Income** = 2 units = 2 × 5000 = Rs. 10000.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 10000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Expenditure** = 50% of **Income**, **Income Increase** = 40%, **Expenditure Increase** = 30%, **Final Saving** = Rs. 7500.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a339a48771c7ed3b9bdf864e43180940e667210daa961b7dc8d47103289d5ed6.png] 

⇒ Let **Initial Income** = 100 units.

⇒ **Initial Expenditure** = 50% of 100 = 50 units.

⇒ **Initial Savings** = 100 − 50 = 50 units.

⇒ **New Income** = 100 + 40% = 140 units.

⇒ **New Expenditure** = 50 + 30% of 50 = 50 + 15 = 65 units.

⇒ **New Savings** = 140 − 65 = 75 units.

⇒ Given **New Savings** = Rs. 7500.

⇒ 75 units = Rs. 7500 ⇒ 1 unit = Rs. 100.

⇒ **Initial Income** = 100 units = 100 × 100 = Rs. 10000.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 10000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

questions.question: The speed of A and B is 50 km/hr and 30 m/s respectively. What is the respective ratio of the distance covered by them in one hour?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **Speed of B** to km/hr: 30 × (18 ÷ 5) = 108 km/hr.

When **time is constant** (1 hour), the **ratio of distances** is equal to the **ratio of speeds**.

Required Ratio = Speed of A : Speed of B = 50 : 108

Divide by 2: 25 : 54

**∴ The correct answer is 25 : 54.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of A = 50 km/hr

Speed of B = 30 m/s

Time = 1 hour

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

1 m/s = 18 ÷ 5 km/hr

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/745832b48562fd213a4784b73f5a9bc536ba7773d2a16985c10a11756c847c9c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Speed of A** = 50 km/hr

⇒ Distance covered by A in 1 hour = 50 × 1 = **50 km**

⇒ **Speed of B** in km/hr = 30 × (18 ÷ 5) = 6 × 18 = **108 km/hr**

⇒ Distance covered by B in 1 hour = 108 × 1 = **108 km**

⇒ Respective **ratio** = Distance A : Distance B

⇒ Ratio = 50 : 108

⇒ Ratio = 25 : 54

**∴ The correct answer is 25 : 54.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **m/s to km/hr**, multiply by 18/5. To convert from **km/hr to m/s**, multiply by 5/18.

Constant Time Property

If time (t) is constant, the **distance (d)** traveled is directly proportional to the **speed (s)**. Thus, d₁/d₂ = s₁/s₂.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed = s₁ − s₂. In **opposite directions**, relative speed = s₁ + s₂.

questions.question: A train crosses a standing pole in 12 seconds and a 550 metre long platform in 22 seconds. What is the length (in metres) and speed (in m/s) of the train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Extra time** taken to cross the **platform** = 22 − 12 = 10 seconds.

In these 10 seconds, the train covers only the **platform length** (550 m).

**Speed** of the train = 550 m ÷ 10 s = 55 m/s.

**Length** of the train = Speed × Time to cross pole = 55 × 12 = 660 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 660 m, 55 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time to cross **pole** (t₁) = 12 sec

Time to cross **platform** (t₂) = 22 sec

Length of **platform** (P) = 550 m

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Calculations:**

Let the **length** of the train be L and its **speed** be S.

When crossing a pole: S = L ÷ 12 → (Eq 1)

When crossing a platform: S = (L + 550) ÷ 22 → (Eq 2)

Equating (Eq 1) and (Eq 2):

⇒ L ÷ 12 = (L + 550) ÷ 22

⇒ L ÷ 6 = (L + 550) ÷ 11

⇒ 11L = 6(L + 550)

⇒ 11L = 6L + 3300

⇒ 5L = 3300

⇒ L = 660 m

Now, calculate **speed** S:

⇒ S = 660 ÷ 12

⇒ S = 55 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 660 m, 55 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Crossing Stationary Objects

When a train crosses a pole or a standing person, the **distance** covered equals the **length** of the train. When it crosses a bridge or platform, the distance is (Length of Train + Length of Platform).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert from **m/s** to **km/h**, multiply by 18/5.

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the **opposite direction**, relative speed = S₁ + S₂. For the **same direction**, relative speed = |S₁ − S₂|.

Were the farmers tilling the fields when the storm hit?

options.text: Were the fields tilled by the farmers when the storm hit?
Had the fields been tilled by the farmers when the storm hit?
Are the fields being tilled by the farmers when the storm hit?
Were the fields being tilled by the farmers when the storm hit?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Were the fields being tilled by the farmers when the storm hit?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The sentence **Were the farmers tilling the fields when the storm hit?** is in the **Active Voice** and follows the **Past Continuous Tense**.

• The structure of an interrogative sentence in the **Past Continuous** active voice is: **Was/Were + Subject + Verb-ing + Object?**

• To convert this into **Passive Voice**, the object of the active sentence (**the fields**) becomes the new subject. Since **the fields** is a plural noun, the auxiliary verb **Were** is placed at the beginning of the sentence.

• The rule for **Past Continuous** passive conversion requires the addition of **being** followed by the **Past Participle (V3)** form of the main verb. Therefore, **tilling** changes to **being tilled**.

• The agent (original subject) **the farmers** is introduced by the preposition **by**.

• The subordinate clause **when the storm hit** is an adverbial of time and remains unchanged in the passive transformation.

• The final passive structure becomes: **Were (Auxiliary) + the fields (Subject) + being + tilled (V3) + by the farmers (Agent) + when the storm hit?**

 **Additional Information__**

• **Tense Mismatch Analysis**:

• **Simple Past Passive**: Uses **Was/Were + V3** without **being**. This represents a completed action rather than an ongoing one, making it unsuitable for translating a continuous active verb.

• **Past Perfect Passive**: Uses **Had + been + V3**. This denotes an action completed before another point in the past, which changes the original meaning of the sentence.

• **Present Continuous Passive**: Uses **Am/Is/Are + being + V3**. This shifts the timeframe from the past to the present, violating the rules of voice conversion where the **tense must remain consistent**.

• In English grammar, **Voice** describes the relationship between the action and the participants. The **Passive Voice** is typically used when the focus is on the action or the recipient rather than the performer.
</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
Will the legal documents have been signed by the partners before the deal is officially announced?

options.text: Are the partners signing the legal documents before the deal is officially announced?
Did the partners sign the legal documents before the deal is officially announced?
Have the partners signed the legal documents before the deal is officially announced?
Will the partners have signed the legal documents before the deal is officially announced?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Will the partners have signed the legal documents before the deal is officially announced?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The provided sentence is in the **Passive Voice** of the **Future Perfect Tense**, which is characterized by the auxiliary verb structure **will + have been + past participle (V3)**.

• To transform this into the **Active Voice**, the **agent** of the action (**the partners**), which follows the preposition **by**, must be moved to the **subject** position at the beginning of the clause.

• The **object** of the passive sentence (**the legal documents**) is moved to the position following the **main verb** in the active construction.

• The verb phrase **will have been signed** is converted to the active form **will have signed**, following the standard **Future Perfect Active** formula: **Subject + will have + V3 + Object**.

• Since the sentence is an **interrogative** (question), the auxiliary verb **Will** must remain at the start of the sentence, followed immediately by the new subject **the partners**.

• The secondary clause, **before the deal is officially announced**, remains unchanged as it serves as a **time-defining subordinate clause** that does not affect the primary voice conversion.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Voice and Tense Consistency**:

• **Active Voice**: Focuses on the **subject** performing the action. For the **Future Perfect Tense**, this always uses **will have + past participle**.

• **Passive Voice**: Focuses on the **object** receiving the action. It always includes the auxiliary **been** between **have** and the **past participle**.

• **Evaluation of Tense Mismatches**:

• **Present Continuous**: Phrases like **Are the partners signing** imply an action currently in progress, which fails to represent the **completion** aspect of the **Perfect Tense**.

• **Simple Past**: Using **Did the partners sign** shifts the timeline to a completed event in the past, losing the **future probability** indicated by **will**.

• **Present Perfect**: The form **Have the partners signed** indicates an action completed at an unspecified time before now, which does not match the **future deadline** context of the original sentence.

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
You are requested to send us a copy of your passport.

options.text: Let a copy of your passport be sent to us.
Send us a copy of your passport.
Please send us a copy of your passport.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Please send us a copy of your passport.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The given sentence **'You are requested to send us a copy of your passport'** is in the **Passive Voice**. It follows the structure of an **imperative sentence** expressing a **request**.

• When converting **passive voice** sentences that begin with **'You are requested to'** into **active voice**, the phrase is replaced with the word **'Please'** to maintain the same **polite tone** and **mood**.

• The verb that follows the infinitive marker **'to'** (which is **'send'**) becomes the **main verb** of the active voice sentence.

• The structure for an **Active Imperative** request is: **Please + Verb (Base Form) + Object/Remaining predicate**. Applying this rule, the sentence becomes **'Please send us a copy of your passport.'**

• The subject **'You'** is implied in **imperative sentences**, which is why it is omitted in the active form.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Imperative Sentences:**

• These sentences are used to express **orders**, **requests**, **suggestions**, or **advice**.

• In **Active Voice**, they usually begin with a **verb** or **'Please'/'Kindly'**.

• In **Passive Voice**, requests are transformed using **'You are requested to'**, while commands often use the **'Let + object + be + past participle'** structure.

• **Evaluation of Other Options:**

• **'Let a copy of your passport be sent to us'**: This is a **Passive Voice** construction using the **'Let'** format, which is typically used for **orders** rather than polite requests.

• **'Send us a copy of your passport'**: This is an **active imperative**, but it functions as a **direct command** and loses the **request nuance** provided by **'requested'** in the original sentence.

• **'We request your passport copy'**: While grammatically active, it changes the **syntactic structure** of the original request and is less common as a direct conversion of an **imperative request**.

</ul

It was rude about the professor's daughter to have rejected the red rose which was being given by the young student.

options.text: rejected the red rose which was
being given by the young student.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the first part of the sentence: **'It was rude about the'**.
 
• In English grammar, when we use an adjective to describe someone's behavior or character in the structure **It + be + adjective + [person] + to-infinitive**, the preposition **'of'** must be used.
 
• Common adjectives used in this pattern include **kind, polite, rude, generous, clever,** and **silly**.
 
• Therefore, the preposition **'about'** should be replaced with **'of'** to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• The correct phrase is **'It was rude of the'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'It was **rude of the** professor's daughter to have rejected the red rose which was being given by the young student.'*

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **professor's daughter to have** – This part is correct. The **perfect infinitive** ('to have rejected') is used to refer to an action that occurred in the past.
 
• **rejected the red rose which was** – This part is grammatically sound, using the **relative pronoun** 'which' to refer back to the rose.
 
• **being given by the young student** – This part correctly uses the **past continuous passive voice** ('was being given') to describe the action performed by the student.
</ul

**Additional Information__**

questions.question: According to the passage, which principle serves as the core foundation of inclusive education?

options.text: To guarantee equal chances for every student, equality should take precedence over equity.
Equity should come before equality to address individual needs before uniformity.
It is important to prioritize teaching approaches that are consistent for all students.
To uphold academic standards, ability-based segregation should be put into place.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage explicitly states that **inclusive education** revolves around the concept of **equity first and then equality**.
 
• This principle implies that students are provided with **supportive services** tailored to their **individual needs** before focusing on uniform treatment.
 
• By prioritizing **equity**, the educational system acknowledges that different learners require different levels of support to reach the same level of **academic excellence** and **well-being**.
 
• The goal of this approach is to enable every student to feel **protected, respected, and confident** so they can grow to their **fullest extent possible**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Equity should come before equality to address individual needs before uniformity.**

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** This is incorrect because the passage prioritizes **equity over equality**, not the other way around.
 
• **Option 3:** Prioritizing **consistent approaches** (uniformity) for all students contradicts the passage's emphasis on **individualized supportive services**.
 
• **Option 4:** The passage promotes students with and without disabilities studying **together** in **general age-appropriate classrooms**, which is the opposite of **ability-based segregation**.
</ul

questions.question: What is the main aim of inclusive education?

options.text: Respect and confidence for every learner
Separate classes and resources for disabled learners

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the passage, **inclusive education** is described as a combination of **pedagogical approaches** and **philosophy**.
 
• Its primary goal is to enable every student to feel **protected**, **respected**, and **confident** in their learning environment.
 
• This foundation allows students to study and grow to their **fullest extent possible**, regardless of their background or disabilities.
 
• Therefore, the main aim is to foster a sense of **respect and confidence** for every learner.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Equal resources for all learners** – While equality is mentioned, the passage emphasizes **equity** first, meaning resources are provided based on **individual needs** rather than just providing the same to everyone.
 
• **Separate classes and resources for disabled learners** – This contradicts the passage, which states all students should study **together** in **general age-appropriate classrooms**.
 
• **Focus only on academics** – The passage highlights a **holistic approach** including **social cohesion**, **belonging**, **active learning**, and **well-being**, rather than just academic excellence.
</ul

questions.question: What role do schools and communities play in implementing inclusive education?

options.text: They should place strong emphasis on competition and high academic achievements over collaboration and diversity
They should only address the needs of students with disabilities as the central focus
They must share ideals that celebrate diversity and promote well-being for all learners
They need to maintain strict uniformity in teaching methods to avoid learning gaps

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **They must share ideals that celebrate diversity and promote well-being for all learners**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the passage, **inclusive education** is successfully implemented in school communities that **celebrate diversity** and support each member’s **well-being**.
 
• The text explicitly states that **communities and schools** will share specific **ideals** and **values** focused on the student’s best interests.
 
• These shared ideals foster an environment of **social cohesion**, **belonging**, and **active learning**, which are essential for the growth of all learners.
 
• The role of these entities is to move beyond mere academic instruction to create a **protected** and **respectful** space for every student.

Therefore, the correct answer is **They must share ideals that celebrate diversity and promote well-being for all learners**.

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Equity vs. Equality:** The foundation of **inclusive education** is the concept of **equity first**, followed by equality, ensuring that individual needs are addressed before applying uniform standards.
 
• **Diverse Classrooms:** It involves students with and without **disabilities** studying together in **age-appropriate classrooms** with **supportive services** tailored to them.
 
• **Holistic Development:** The philosophy aims to enable every student to grow to their **fullest extent** by encouraging positive interactions with **peers** and the wider **school community**.
 
• **Critique of Other Options:** Strategies that emphasize **competition** or **strict uniformity** are contrary to the inclusive values of **collaboration** and **individualized support** mentioned in the text.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following describes the inclusive education philosophy the best?

options.text: Providing students with equal opportunities without recognizing their individual learning needs or differences
Encouraging segregation of students to target specific academic outcomes and improve classroom management
Integrating diverse teaching strategies and inclusive values to foster students' holistic development
Limiting social interactions among students to minimize conflicts

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Integrating diverse teaching strategies and inclusive values to foster students' holistic development**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the passage, **inclusive education** is defined as a combination of **pedagogical approaches** and **philosophy**.
 
• It emphasizes **equity first** and then equality, ensuring that students receive **supportive services** tailored to their **individual needs**.
 
• The philosophy aims for more than just academic success; it focuses on **holistic development** by making every student feel **protected, respected, and confident**.
 
• By integrating **inclusive values** like **social cohesion**, **belonging**, and **active learning**, schools create an environment where all students study together in **general age-appropriate classrooms**.
 
• Thus, the best description of this philosophy is the integration of diverse strategies and values to foster the **fullest growth** of every learner.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Integrating diverse teaching strategies and inclusive values to foster students' holistic development**.

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** This is incorrect because the passage explicitly states that students are provided with services in accordance with their **individual needs**, rather than ignoring them.
 
• **Option 2:** This contradicts the core principle of inclusion, which requires students with and without disabilities to **study together** in the same classroom, rather than being **segregated**.
 
• **Option 4:** The passage encourages **positive interactions** with peers and members of the school community, not the limitation of social interactions.
</ul

questions.question: Which is NOT a value of inclusive education?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Segregation by ability**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the passage, **inclusive education** is built upon the philosophy that all students, with or without **disabilities**, should study **together** in general **age-appropriate classrooms**.
 
• The text explicitly lists several values and beliefs that form the foundation of this approach, including **social cohesion**, **belonging**, and **active learning**.
 
• The goal is to foster an environment where every student feels **protected, respected, and confident**, allowing them to grow to their **fullest extent possible**.
 
• **Segregation by ability** implies separating students based on their skill levels or disabilities, which is the direct opposite of the **inclusive** model described, where students study together.
 
• Therefore, **segregation by ability** is NOT a value of inclusive education.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Segregation by ability**.

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Social cohesion:** This is a stated value in the passage that results from **positive interactions** with peers and the school community.
 
• **Active learning:** The passage identifies this as a core belief focused on the **student's best interests** and a full school experience.
 
• **Sense of belonging:** The text highlights **belonging** as a crucial element that helps students feel integrated rather than isolated.
 
• **Segregation by ability:** This practice involves grouping students into different environments based on their **academic performance** or **physical/mental capabilities**, which contradicts the principle of **equity first** and **celebrating diversity** mentioned in the text.
</ul
